t: Emperor Shōmu ordered the Great Buddha in 743 after smallpox, bad harvests and a rebellion had left Japan unsettled, and made Tōdai-ji the head of the provincial temples.
In the Nara period it was the central administrative temple for the provincial temples and for six Buddhist schools, and all officially licensed monks were ordained there.
The Great Buddha Hall has been rebuilt twice after fire; the present hall, finished in 1709, is a third smaller than its predecessor and was given a steel frame between 1974 and 1980.
dyk: The 752 eye-opening ceremony for the Great Buddha was attended by 10,000 monks and 4,000 dancers, and the project used much of Japan's bronze and relied entirely on imported gold.
ev: Kinshōsen-ji, the forerunner of Tōdai-ji, was established as a gesture of appeasement for the troubled spirit of Prince Motoi
Emperor Shōmu commanded that a very large Buddha image be built, and work began at Shigaraki
The eye-opening ceremony celebrating the completion of the Great Buddha was held
Ganjin, who had reached Japan after six attempts to cross the sea, gave ordination at Tōdai-ji to Empress Kōken, former Emperor Shōmu and others
The head of the Great Buddha fell to the ground, and gifts from across the empire paid for a new head
Minamoto Yoritomo initiated a reconstruction, entrusted to the monk Chogen
The present Great Buddha Hall was finished
A second large-scale restoration, begun in 1974 and using steel framing, was completed

f.made: Commissioned by Emperor Shōmu after a run of disasters and epidemics; the monk Gyōki and his pupils gathered donations, and the temple's records say more than 2,600,000 people contributed
f.form: A Buddhist temple complex built in imitation of Tang dynasty temples; its Great Buddha Hall is 57 metres long, 50 wide and 49 high and holds a bronze Vairocana, 14.98 metres high by the temple's own figures, weighing 500 tonnes
f.where: In the city of Nara, Japan, as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
f.known: the Great Buddha (Daibutsu) of Vairocana; the Great Buddha Hall; the Nio guardians of the Great South Gate; the Shōsōin storehouse; ordination under the Vinaya; headquarters of the Kegon school
